question.content:
Tony tried to define a translation.

- Point $A$ maps to point $A'$.
- Every point $P$ maps to point $P'$ such that $\overrightarrow{PP'}$ is parallel to $\overrightarrow{AA'}$ and points in the same direction as $\overrightarrow{AA'}$.

**What mistake did Tony make in his definition of a translation?**

[[☃ radio 1]]

choices.clue: A translation doesn't have a center.
choices.content: Tony needed to mention that the center of translation maps to itself.

choices.clue: If $\overline{PP'}$ and $\overline{AA'}$ can have different lengths, there would be infinitely many possible points for $P'$.
choices.content: $\overline{PP'}$ must have the same length as $\overline{AA'}$.

choices.clue: A translation moves all points in the same direction, so we need $\overrightarrow{PP'}$ to be parallel to $\overrightarrow{AA'}$
There is more than one possible point $P'$ we could draw from Tony's definition. What additional information does the definition need to clarify which point is the image of point $P$?
choices.content: Tony did not make a mistake.
